_: Hand-written half of the Maps pages (Oct 30 2026). scripts/valorant-maps.py joins it with valorant-api.com's /v1/maps (pictures, callouts, sites, in-game coordinates) and writes /valorant/maps/. Order = newest first inside each mode (ties keep this file's order, which is Riot's maps page). released = the wiki's date (Riot's patch notes for Summit); real = the wiki's decoded coordinates. Guides: every tip was checked against a reference (Riot 13.00 notes, the fandom wiki's mechanics, THE SPIKE / KeenGamer / esports guides); Adrian has the final say. A new map: add its entry, run the script.

competitive.name: Competitive
competitive.title: Competitive maps
competitive.jett: Maps in today's ranked pool come first, then every other map, newest first. Me? I practise all of them.

tdm.name: Team Deathmatch
tdm.title: Team Deathmatch
tdm.jett: Small arenas, fast respawns, first team to 100 kills wins. Perfect warm-up before ranked, I do it every day!

other.name: Other modes
other.title: Other modes
other.jett: Skirmish, the new Gauntlet arena and the practice maps. No rank on the line, so go wild.

mode_info.tdm: Team Deathmatch is 5v5: first team to 100 kills, or the most kills after 9.5 minutes. The match runs in four stages that unlock better guns, weapon spawners hand out more, and you respawn 1.5 seconds after dying.
mode_info.skirmish: Skirmish is an elimination mode on one small arena with different cover layouts. Its matchmade 2v2 (from patch 12.03) is first to 10 rounds with random agents and no abilities; in custom games it runs up to 5v5.

maps.name: Summit
maps.blurb: A Radiant training academy hidden in the mountains of China, with training halls and meditation gardens. Two sites, three lanes, and three walls that drop for the rest of the round.

guide.intro: A is the smaller site and B the bigger one. Mid's Fountain links both, and each of A, mid and B has a wall that either team can drop.
tricks: Three droppable walls: one on A, one in mid and one on B.
Shoot a wall's switch to drop it. Once it falls it stays down until the round ends.
A dropped wall closes that route for both teams: it can stop a rotation, a flank, or your own retake.

sites.name: A
attack: Clear Garden and the boxes before you plant, and smoke the defender side the retake comes from.
Send part of the team through A Link from mid while the rest walks A Main: a split beats one crowded choke.
defend: Don't sit deep on A alone. It's the small site and a full hit takes it fast.
Drop the A wall to slow a hit, or to cut off attackers who are already inside.

sites.name: B
attack: Clear Close Box and the deep corners before planting. B is the big site with the most angles.
Plant first, then drop the B wall so the retake has fewer ways in.
defend: Drop the B wall to slow a B rush or block a split from mid.
Tower, Trophy and Gym are the deeper defender spots on B.

sites.name: Mid
attack: Take Fountain with smokes, flashes or recon, never a dry peek: it opens both sites.
Drop the mid wall once you've picked your site, so defenders can't rotate through mid.
defend: Keep one player on mid every round.
Wait for information before you drop a wall: an early drop can lock your own rotators out.

maps.name: Corrode
maps.blurb: A French castle town turned radianite salt mine. Two sites, three lanes and no gadgets at all: just medieval streets, mining machinery and a lot of angles.

guide.intro: Corrode is a classic two-site, three-lane map. Mid is narrow and packed with cover, and it's the lane for lurks and quick rotations.
tricks: No doors, ropes or teleporters: Corrode is the second standard map with no mechanics (Pearl was the first).
Both sites sit low, so defenders often get to shoot down at you from above.

sites.name: All sites
attack: Pressure mid first, then split into a site from two sides instead of all five through one choke.
On a B hit, smoke B Tower and B Link before you walk in.
defend: Call contact and how many you see before anyone rotates.
Watch mid for lurkers: it's the short way to a flank.

sites.name: Mid
attack: Mid control is the key fight here: win it and you can hit either site.

maps.name: Abyss
maps.blurb: A secret base at the bottom of an endless chasm. No outer walls: step off an edge and you fall to your death.

guide.intro: The first map with no outer walls. Edges, a drop in mid and narrow ledges change how every fight near the rim plays out.
tricks: No outer walls, and a drop in mid: fall off and you die.
Danger (B) and Secret (A) are narrow ledges on the rim, used as jump shortcuts.
Catwalk is reached only by jumping the mid drop to an ascender, from Top or Library.
Ropes: A Site up to A Tower, B Main up to Mid Bend, and one in attacker spawn.
Both Vent entrances have doors with 120 HP. Break one and it stays open for the round.

sites.name: A
attack: Break a Vent door before you need it: it's a second way in that stays open all round.
Secret's ledge reaches A from an angle defenders forget, but one bad jump is a death.
defend: A Tower looks down over A Site, and the rope from the site takes you straight up.
A Vent door breaking is a warning: someone is coming through Vent.

sites.name: B
attack: Danger's ledge is a shortcut onto B, but miss the jump and you're dead.
defend: Fight away from the edges: a knockback or a bad step there ends your round.

sites.name: Mid
attack: The rope from B Main up to Mid Bend links B to mid: use it to join a mid push.
defend: Catwalk is reached from both Top and Library: watch both ways up.

maps.name: Sunset
maps.blurb: A disaster at a Kingdom facility threatens a whole Los Angeles neighbourhood. Grab a bite at the food truck, then fight across three lanes.

guide.intro: A traditional two-site, three-lane map. Its one gadget is the door between B Market and Mid Courtyard.
tricks: The door between B Market and Mid Courtyard opens and closes with a switch on the Market side.
Closed, the door stops bullets, but it has 500 HP. Break it and it stays open for the round.
With the door gone, there's a long sightline from B Site into mid.

sites.name: A
attack: A is tight corridors and close fights: flash the near corners before you swing.

sites.name: B
attack: Break the Market door from mid to open a second way onto B.
defend: Close the Market door to cut mid's route into B: attackers need 500 damage to get through.

sites.name: Mid
attack: Mid is a horseshoe with lots of ways in: take it as a group with utility, not alone.
defend: Watch Courtyard: it's mid's shortcut into B Market through the door.

maps.name: Lotus
maps.blurb: A mysterious structure built around an astral conduit, deep in the Indian jungle. Three sites, rotating stone doors and a wall you can break.

guide.intro: Three sites, so defenders are spread thin. Two rotating doors and a breakable wall decide how fast anyone gets from one site to another.
tricks: Two rotating doors: one between A Main and A Tree, one between C Mound and B Main. A button on either side spins them.
A turning door is loud and shows on the map for everyone.
The wall between A Main and A Link has 400 HP. Break it to open a new path for the round.
A rope at the back of A Site goes up to A Top, and walking off A Top down to A Drop makes no sound.

sites.name: A
attack: Split A from A Main and A Tree at once, so defenders can't hold both.
Smoke A Top, Drop and Stairs: that's where the A defenders play.
defend: Choke A Main and A Tree, and leave a trap or turret for flanks.
Walk, don't run, off A Top: land close to the edge and nobody hears it.

sites.name: B
attack: B is all angles: go in only with strong smokes and clear calls.
defend: Smoke B Main to stall the push, then retake with your team.

sites.name: C
attack: Flash C Main or Mound before you peek: an Operator often waits there.
Plant near Waterfall or Hall so you can guard the spike without peeking.
defend: Make C Main your choke point.

sites.name: Retakes
attack: A door that stays silent tells you nobody is rotating through it.
defend: Don't stack all five on a retake: send one player around the back.

maps.name: Pearl
maps._spots: valorant-api puts most of Pearl's callouts beside the corridors they name (stale since its rework; no single shift fixes it, checked Oct 30 2026): only sites + spawns go on the map
maps.blurb: A two-site map in a vibrant underwater city in Lisbon. No gadgets: the streets, plazas and long sightlines are the whole fight.

guide.intro: Riot's first map with no mechanics at all. Long lanes favour rifles and the Operator, and mid control decides the round.
tricks: No doors, ropes or teleporters.
Long sightlines everywhere: rifles and the Operator do well here.

sites.name: A
attack: Clear Secret and A Link as you come in: that's where A defenders hide.
defend: Hold A from Secret or A Link.

sites.name: B
attack: Check B Tower before you commit to the site.
defend: Hold B Tower against a B Main push: attackers clear the low angles first.

sites.name: Mid
attack: Win mid and you can hit either site, or cut behind the defenders.
defend: A trap or turret near your spawn warns you of a flank.

maps.name: Fracture
maps.blurb: A top-secret research facility split in two by a failed radianite experiment. Defenders spawn in the middle, attackers can hit a site from both sides.

guide.intro: An H-shaped map: the sites are on opposite sides, defenders spawn between them, and attackers use ziplines to reach the far side and pinch.
tricks: Attackers spawn in one place but reach the far side on two one-way ziplines that pass under defender spawn.
During the buy phase, defenders can't hear attackers on the ziplines.
On a zipline you can't stop, turn back, use abilities or let go.
If the spike carrier dies on a zipline, the spike lands on the nearer side.
A Hall's door opens by itself, loudly, when anyone gets close, from either side.
Four ult orbs, one in each quarter of the map.

sites.name: A
attack: Hit A from both sides at once: A Main, and A Dish across the zipline.
defend: A Hall's door opens loudly when someone nears it. That's a free warning.

sites.name: B
attack: Pinch B from B Main and B Arcade together.
defend: Hold from B Tower, and use smokes or walls to slow a fast rotation through the site.

sites.name: Rotations
attack: Use the ziplines to fake one site and arrive at the other.
defend: You spawn between the sites, so your rotations are short: give up space and retake together.

maps.name: Breeze
maps.blurb: Ruins and tropical beaches on an island in the Bermuda Triangle. The biggest, most open map in the game: wide spaces and long fights.

guide.intro: Breeze is wide open, so long-range fights decide it. The rope on A and the automatic door in mid are its only gadgets.
tricks: The largest and most open map: bring rifles and the Operator.
A rope at the back of A Site lifts defenders up to Bridge and Hall.
Mid Hall's door opens by itself, loudly, from either side, and for anything thrown at it.

sites.name: A
attack: Push A from two sides: part of the team on the main path, the rest through Mid Hall.
defend: Keep someone near Hall so A doesn't get flanked.
The rope up to Bridge is your fast rotation off A.

sites.name: B
attack: Hit B from B Main and Mid Top together, so the defenders have to split.
defend: One player on site, one in Mid Nest watching mid.

sites.name: Mid
attack: When nobody holds Mid Nest, push through Wood Doors.
defend: Always keep someone in Mid Nest to call mid pushes.

maps.name: Icebox
maps.blurb: A secret Kingdom dig site swallowed by the Arctic. Ziplines, ropes and stacked containers make every fight a fight for height.

guide.intro: Icebox is all about height. Both sites have raised spots, and ropes and ziplines get you up to them.
tricks: The A zipline was the first horizontal zipline in the game.
Both sites have raised spots you climb by rope, and the spike can be planted up there.
High ground matters here: most fights are about height.

sites.name: A
attack: Clear the high spots first: Rafters, Nest and Pipes, before you plant.
defend: Play the high ground: it's the strongest angle on A.

sites.name: B
attack: Recon B before you walk in: the containers hide a lot of corners.
defend: Tube is a sneaky way to get a second angle on the B push.

sites.name: Mid
attack: Taking mid needs the player there alive: if they die early, the team is split.
defend: One player holds mid, and Kitchen is the fast way to back them up.

maps.name: Ascent
maps.blurb: A Venetian square where a huge open mid splits two sites, and each site has a door that can shut it off.

guide.intro: The open mid decides the round, and each site's door can shut off one way in, for either team.
tricks: Each site has a door (A Link on A, Market on B) that starts open. Its switch is on the site side: next to the door on A, on a table in Toolshed on B.
Closed, a door stops bullets, but it has 500 HP. Break it and it stays open for the round.
The two walls between Courtyard and Link have 400 HP panels. Break one and you can shoot through it for the round.
A Window's glass breaks on the first bullet or thrown ability.

sites.name: A
attack: After you plant, close the A Link door: the retake from mid has one way less.
defend: Close the A Link door to stop a push from mid into A.

sites.name: B
attack: Plant, then close the Market door from Toolshed so the retake can't come through Market.
defend: Boat House gives a cross angle on B Main.

sites.name: Mid
attack: Smoke Catwalk and Top, then send recon: mid control opens both sites.
defend: Break the Courtyard panels early if you want to spray through the walls into Link.

maps.name: Split
maps.blurb: Two sites split by a tall centre in the heart of Tokyo. Ropes and vents take you up, and a tower looms over each site.

guide.intro: Split is vertical: a raised mid and a tower on each site. It was the first map with ropes.
tricks: Ropes: two from Sewer up to A Lobby, one from B Hell up to B Tower, and four that run through Vent.
Each site has a tower looming over it.

sites.name: A
attack: Expect defenders up high: clear Rafters, Screens and the site boxes, and scout before you walk on.
defend: Slow the A push with a wall, a trap or a turret, then fight what gets through.

sites.name: B
attack: Clear B Back, Stairs and Garage before you plant: that's where B defenders hide.
defend: Delay B with smokes and retake as a group.

sites.name: Mid
attack: Clear Vent, Mail and the ropes: that's where mid defenders sit.
defend: Listen for audio cues before you rotate.

maps.name: Haven
maps.blurb: A forgotten monastery in Bhutan, and the first map with three sites to fight over.

guide.intro: Three sites means defenders are thin everywhere. Attackers win by finding the weak one fast, and defenders by rotating faster.
tricks: The first map with three sites.
In mid, the Garage doors and part of the Window wall have 400 HP panels. Break them and you can shoot through for the round.
Two ult orbs: one in A Long, one in C Long.

sites.name: A
attack: Hit A from A Long and Sewer at once, with smokes on A Tower and the defender side.
defend: Smoke A Long or Sewer to slow the push.

sites.name: B
attack: B is reached through mid: take mid control first, then the site.
defend: B is the hardest site to hold: a wall or a slow at the mid entrance stops a rush.

sites.name: C
attack: Enter C from C Long or Garage, and flash before you swing.
defend: Leave a Sentinel on C with traps and a turret, and let them come.

maps.name: Bind
maps.blurb: Two sites, no middle. A Moroccan desert town where two one-way teleporters are the fastest way across.

guide.intro: Bind has no mid. Two one-way teleporters link the sites instead, and every teleport is heard across the map.
tricks: Two one-way teleporters: A Short to B Short, and B Long to A Lobby.
Every teleport makes a sound the whole map hears.
The exit door opens only from inside, but bullets go through it.
Abilities, the spike and dropped guns can go through a teleporter too.

sites.name: A
attack: Hit A from Bath and A Short together.
Teleport from B Long to fake B, then arrive in A Lobby.
defend: Hear a teleport? Someone is on the move: call it and adjust.

sites.name: B
attack: Enter B from Long and Window at once, so defenders can't hold both.
defend: Slow the jump down from B Window with a slow or a wall.

maps.name: Glitch
maps.blurb: A Team Deathmatch arena modelled on China's Tianmen Mountains. Like every TDM map, it's a simulation Max Bot built to hunt the agents.

maps.name: Drift
maps.blurb: A Team Deathmatch arena modelled on Thailand. Like every TDM map, it's a simulation Max Bot built to hunt the agents.

maps.name: District
maps.blurb: One of the first three Team Deathmatch arenas, dressed like Split. A simulation built by Max Bot, so it's set in no real place.

maps.name: Kasbah
maps.blurb: One of the first three Team Deathmatch arenas, dressed like Bind. A simulation built by Max Bot, so it's set in no real place.

maps.name: Piazza
maps.blurb: One of the first three Team Deathmatch arenas, dressed like Ascent. A simulation built by Max Bot, so it's set in no real place.

maps.name: Gauntlet
maps.blurb: The arena of Gauntlet: Glitched, the 16-player mode where eight duos draft and upgrade abilities between short 2v2 rounds.

maps.name: Skirmish
maps.blurb: One small arena with five cover layouts (A to E), made for Skirmish's quick elimination rounds.

maps.name: Basic Training
maps.blurb: The tutorial every new account starts with: Brimstone, Jett, Sova and Sage teach the basics in the Range, then planting and defusing in a simulated Haven.

maps.name: The Range
maps.blurb: The practice ground on floating Venetian islands: every agent unlocked, a shooting range with bots, and target boards from 5 to 50 metres.
